subtitle: Silver, Thread and the Quiet Engine of Mandu

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over Mandu fort, slowly tightening on a hand spilling silver coins onto fine cotton
panels.action: Malwa’s Merchant-Minter stands on a Mandu bastion at dusk, one hand letting silver coins tumble onto a folded length of sheer Chanderi cloth laid on the parapet, the black-soil plain and distant trade roads stretching below.

dialogue.text: In Mandu’s age of stone palaces, it was not kings but unknown merchants and minters whose silver coins and cotton cloth kept Shadiabad alive.

i18n.hi: मांडू के पत्थर महलों के दौर में, राजे नहीं, अनजान सौदागर और सिक्के ढालने वाले ही चांदी के सिक्कों और सूती कपड़े से शादीआबाद को जिंदा रखते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in from the dark Narmada valley to sunlit Malwa plateau fields
panels.action: From the misty Narmada valley, the view rises to the Malwa plateau, where Malwa’s Merchant-Minter surveys vast fields of black soil furrowed with green cotton plants, bullocks plodding as peasants work under a wide sky.

dialogue.text: On Malwa’s high black-soil plateau, long before the Malwa sultans, farmers coaxed cotton from crackled earth and sent it down dusty tracks to older markets.

i18n.hi: मालवा के ऊँचे, काले मिट्टी वाले पठार पर, सुल्तानों से बहुत पहले, किसान फटी धरती से कपास उगाकर पुराने बाज़ारों तक धूल भरी राहों से भेजते थे।

panels.shot: medium wide along a caravan road, low-angle tracking beside pack animals
panels.action: Malwa’s Merchant-Minter walks beside a camel caravan loaded with bales of cotton and bundles of cloth, the road signposted by scattered shrines as the track winds toward the hill city of Mandu perched on the horizon.

dialogue.text: When Malwa broke from Delhi around 1401, these same tracks began to feed a new hill capital—Shadiabad, the City of Joy—where rulers, priests and soldiers all needed pay and cloth.

i18n.hi: जब 1401 के आस-पास मालवा दिल्ली से अलग हुआ, वही रास्ते नई पहाड़ी राजधानी शादीआबाद – खुशी का शहर – को भरने लगे, जहाँ राजा, पुजारी और सिपाही सबको मज़दूरी और कपड़ा चाहिए था।

panels.shot: interior wide of Mandu bazaar, bustling, slight high angle
panels.action: Inside a crowded Mandu bazaar courtyard, Malwa’s Merchant-Minter stands at a stall piled with cotton yarn, coarse cloth and shining silver tankas, surrounded by townsfolk haggling as palace walls rise beyond.

dialogue.text: Markets flowered under Mandu’s fortified ridge—coarse cotton for soldiers, finer cloth for court, grain for the kitchens, all meeting under arches of stone and under the eyes of tax-collectors.

i18n.hi: मांडू की किलेबंद पहाड़ी के नीचे मंडियां फूलीं—सिपाहियों के लिए मोटा सूत, दरबार के लिए महीन कपड़ा, रसोइयों के लिए अनाज—सब पत्थर की मेहराबों तले, महसूल वालों की नज़र में।

panels.shot: close-up of hands weighing and exchanging coins and cloth
panels.action: A close view shows Malwa’s Merchant-Minter weighing a piece of fine cotton in one pan and placing a neat stack of square silver tankas in the other as a weaver watches anxiously in a dim shop.

dialogue.text: By the fifteenth century, silver tankas of Malwa—square, bright and carefully weighed—moved from weaver to broker to tax official, turning thread into revenue.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी तक मालवा के चाँदी के टंके—चौकोर, चमकदार, तौलकर बनाए—जुलाहों से दलालों और महसूलदारों तक घूमते, धागे को खजाने में बदलते थे।

panels.shot: moody interior of a mint, diagonal composition with furnaces and anvils
panels.action: Inside a low stone mint hall at Mandu, Malwa’s Merchant-Minter stands near a furnace as workers pour molten silver into molds, others hammer blanks between dies on an anvil, sparks glowing against dark walls.

dialogue.text: Behind the bazaar’s noise, the Mandu mint turned bullion into trust—silver melted, cast, and struck with the names of Malwa’s sultans and the hill city Shadiabad.

i18n.hi: बाज़ार की हलचल के पीछे, मांडू की टकसाल चांदी की सिल्लियों को भरोसे में बदलती—धातु पिघलती, ढलती, और उस पर मालवा के सुल्तानों और पहाड़ी नगरी शादीआबाद के नाम ठोक दिए जाते।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a freshly struck coin in tongs
panels.action: In a tight close-up, Malwa’s Merchant-Minter holds a just-struck square tanka in iron tongs, its face showing Arabic-Persian script, while on the edge of another coin nearby faint Nagari letters curve along the margin.

dialogue.text: Some issues bore only Persian and Arabic, others added Nagari—pragmatic marks for a land where clerks, money-changers and villagers read in more than one script.

i18n.hi: कुछ सिक्कों पर सिर्फ़ फ़ारसी और अरबी, तो कुछ पर साथ में नागरी भी—ऐसे निशान जो उस देस के लिए थे जहाँ बाबू, सर्राफ़ और गाँव वाले कई लिपियों में पढ़ते थे।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of a scribe at a low desk in the mint
panels.action: From behind Malwa’s Merchant-Minter, we see a scribe at a low desk in the mint, copying accounts in Persian while a Hindu clerk beside him jots numbers in Nagari on a waxed tablet, coin sacks stacked between them.

dialogue.text: The bilingual coins echoed a bilingual bureaucracy—Ain and ledgers in Persian, local tallies and promises in Nagari—stitched together by habit more than by slogan.

i18n.hi: ये दोभाषी सिक्के एक दोभाषी अफ़सरशाही की गूँज थे—आइन और बहीख़ाते फ़ारसी में, और देसी हिसाब-किताब, उधार-पर्चे नागरी में—नारे से नहीं, रोज़ की आदत से सिलकर जोड़े गए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Chanderi hillside town, morning mist lifting
panels.action: On a misty hillside townscape of Chanderi, tiled roofs and temple spires rise around a modest fort, as Malwa’s Merchant-Minter stands on a terrace overlooking lanes where bundles of cloth hang from balconies.

dialogue.text: To the northeast lay Chanderi, an old weaving town whose fame for fine cotton predated the Malwa sultans, yet whose looms hummed louder as court orders and traders’ demands grew.

i18n.hi: उत्तरे-पूर्व में था चंदेरी, पुराना बुनाई कस्बा, जिसका महीन सूती कपड़ा मालवा के सुल्तानों से भी पहले मशहूर था, पर दरबारी हुक्म और सौदागरों की माँग से उसके करघे और ज़ोर से गूँजने लगे।

panels.shot: intimate interior of a weaver’s house, low-angle toward loom and spinning
panels.action: Inside a Chanderi home, Malwa’s Merchant-Minter watches a family at work—one woman spinning cotton on a charkha, another winding thread, while a man at a handloom weaves a gauzy fabric that catches the light.

dialogue.text: Weaving stayed a household craft—women spinning, men at looms—yet middlemen linked these rooms to Mandu’s courtyards, and beyond to ports and caravans.

i18n.hi: बुनाई घरों की ही कला रही—औरतें कताई पर, मर्द करघों पर—पर बिचौलिये इन्हीं कमरों को मांडू के आंगनों से, और आगे बंदरगाहों और काफ़िलों से जोड़ते रहे।

panels.shot: mid-shot of merchant negotiating with weavers, coins and cloth visible
panels.action: Malwa’s Merchant-Minter sits cross-legged opposite the weaver, unrolling a sample of translucent cloth while placing a small bag of coins on the floor between them as both weigh quality against price with careful eyes.

dialogue.speaker: Malwa’s Merchant-Minter
dialogue.text: Finer thread, tighter weave, and I will pay in silver, not copper.

i18n.hi: धागा नाजुक, बुनाई कसी, तो तुझे चांदी दूँगा, तांबा नहीं।

panels.shot: map-like bird's-eye of routes from Malwa to Gujarat and Deccan, overlaid with caravans
panels.action: From high above, stylised roads radiate from Ujjain and Chanderi toward the west and south, dotted with tiny caravans; Malwa’s Merchant-Minter stands over a floor map, tracing a route toward a hazy sea coast.

dialogue.text: Routes from Ujjain and Chanderi ran to Gujarat’s ports and to the Deccan; Malwa’s cloth and coin travelled with grain, horses and spices toward ships and other sultanates.

i18n.hi: उज्जैन और चंदेरी से राहें गुजरात के बंदरगाहों और दक्खन की तरफ जातीं; मालवा का कपड़ा और सिक्के अनाज, घोड़ों और मसालों के साथ जहाज़ों और दूसरे सुल्तानों की ओर बढ़ते।

panels.shot: dynamic road-level shot of caravan halted at a toll gate with armed guards
panels.action: At a narrow pass, Malwa’s Merchant-Minter stands with his halted caravan before a timbered toll gate manned by spear-bearing soldiers, a revenue officer holding a tally-stick while armed horsemen watch from a rocky ledge.

dialogue.text: Along those roads, trade meant tax and risk—customs posts, river ferries, rival chiefs and sultanates fighting over the right to squeeze coin from moving bales.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं सड़कों पर सौदा मतलब महसूल और ख़तरा—चौकियाँ, नदी के घाट, दुश्मन सरदार और सुल्तानियाँ जो चलते गठ्ठरों से सिक्का निचोड़ने के हक़ पर लड़ती थीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of battlefield in the distance with smoke, foreground caravan turning aside
panels.action: In the distance, faint smoke rises from a battlefield where banners clash; in the foreground, Malwa’s Merchant-Minter signals his caravan to turn onto a lesser track, pack animals hesitating at the fork.

dialogue.text: Wars with Gujarat, the Lodis, and later the Mughals were fought partly over these same corridors—control of roads, ferries, markets and their steady stream of silver.

i18n.hi: गुजरात, लोदी और बाद में मुगलों से जंगें भी इन्हीं गलियारों पर थीं—सड़कों, घाटों, बाज़ारों और उनकी बहती चांदी की धारा पर क़ब्ज़े की लड़ाई।

panels.shot: quiet interior of a revenue office, low light, scrolls and coins stacked
panels.action: In a dim Mandu revenue office, Malwa’s Merchant-Minter stands as officials count coins into heaps beside bundles of cloth and grain receipts, a wall map marking villages with tiny pegs.

dialogue.text: Later, Abu’l-Fazl would list Malwa’s lands, its cotton, and, by then, its opium for the Mughal emperor—proof that these fields and markets kept feeding larger empires.

i18n.hi: बाद में अबुल-फ़ज़्ल ने मुग़ल बादशाह के लिए मालवा की ज़मीनें, उसकी कपास, और तब तक उग चुका उसका अफ़ीम गिना—सबूत कि ये खेत और मंडियां बड़े साम्राज्यों को खिलाती रहीं।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of Mandu palaces fading into Mughal camp, then into ruins
panels.action: A wide view shows Mandu’s palaces first lit and busy, then overlaid with a Mughal military camp at their foot, and finally the same walls centuries later, half-ruined and silent; Malwa’s Merchant-Minter stands unchanged in the foreground, holding an old coin and a piece of cloth.

dialogue.text: Mandu fell in 1562 and Malwa’s sultans vanished into chronicles, but their coins kept circulating, their fields stayed planted, and the looms of Chanderi did not fall silent.

i18n.hi: 1562 में मांडू गिरा और मालवा के सुल्तान तारीख़ों में गुम हो गए, पर उनके सिक्के चलन में रहे, उनके खेत जोते जाते रहे, और चंदेरी के करघे खामोश नहीं हुए।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a worn Malwa coin and fragment of Chanderi cloth in palm
panels.action: In a close-up, Malwa’s Merchant-Minter’s weathered palm cradles a worn Malwa silver tanka and a delicate strip of Chanderi cloth, both aged yet intact, the faint outline of Mandu’s walls blurred in the background.

dialogue.text: Behind every ruined palace stand unseen hands—farmers of black soil, weavers of fine cotton, and minters of square silver—without whom Malwa’s kings would have ruled over empty stone.

i18n.hi: हर खंडहर महल के पीछे अनदेखे हाथ खड़े हैं—काली मिट्टी के किसान, महीन सूती के बुनकर, और चौकोर चांदी के सिक्के ढालने वाले—जिनके बिना मालवा के राजा खाली पत्थर पर राज करते।

title_i18n.hi: शादीआबाद के सिक्के, चंदेरी का कपड़ा

subtitle_i18n.en: Silver, Thread and the Quiet Engine of Mandu
subtitle_i18n.hi: चांदी, धागा और मांडू की खामोश चक्की
